QuestionText: The liquid medium of blood that carries dissolved substances is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Plasma is the straw-coloured liquid component of blood (~55%) that transports nutrients, hormones, and waste products.

QuestionText: Red blood cells (RBCs) contain ___ which carries oxygen
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Haemoglobin (Hb) is the iron-containing protein in RBCs that binds and transports O2 from lungs to tissues.

QuestionText: White blood cells (WBCs) are important for
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: WBCs (leucocytes) form the immune system's defence against pathogens.

QuestionText: Platelets are important for
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments that aggregate at wound sites and initiate blood clotting.

QuestionText: The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from heart to body is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: The aorta is the largest artery, carrying oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the entire body.

QuestionText: Veins carry blood ___ the heart
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Veins carry blood back toward the heart. Most veins carry deoxygenated blood (except pulmonary veins).

QuestionText: Arteries carry blood ___ the heart
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body tissues.

QuestionText: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels where
Options: A) Exchange of materials between blood and tissues occurs
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Capillaries have walls only one cell thick, allowing exchange of O2, CO2, nutrients, and waste with surrounding tissues.

QuestionText: The human heart has ___ chambers
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Human heart: 2 atria (upper) + 2 ventricles (lower) = 4 chambers.

QuestionText: The right side of the heart pumps blood to the
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs for oxygenation.

QuestionText: The left side of the heart pumps blood to the
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood from lungs → left ventricle → aorta → body.

QuestionText: The heart valve between left atrium and left ventricle is the
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: The mitral (bicuspid) valve on the left side and tricuspid on the right prevent backflow from ventricle to atrium.

QuestionText: A normal resting human heart rate is approximately
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Normal resting heart rate: 60-100 bpm (average ~72 bpm).

QuestionText: Blood pressure is highest in
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Arteries receive blood directly from the ventricles at high pressure; pressure decreases in capillaries and veins.

QuestionText: In plants, xylem tissue transports
Options: A) Water and mineral salts from roots to leaves
B) Glucose from leaves to roots
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals unidirectionally upward from roots to all aerial parts.

QuestionText: In plants, phloem tissue transports
Options: A) Food (sucrose) from leaves to all parts
B) Water from roots to leaves
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Phloem translocates organic nutrients (mainly sucrose) from photosynthesising leaves to all plant parts.

QuestionText: Transpiration creates a pulling force called
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Transpiration pull (cohesion-tension): evaporation of water from leaves creates tension that pulls water up xylem.

QuestionText: Root pressure occurs because
Options: A) Minerals are actively absorbed, drawing water in by osmosis
B) Water is pumped by the heart
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Active mineral uptake by roots lowers solute potential, drawing water in by osmosis, creating positive root pressure.

QuestionText: The guttation phenomenon in plants is
Options: A) Exudation of water droplets from leaf tips due to root pressure
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Guttation: root pressure forces water out through hydathodes at leaf margins/tips, visible as water droplets in the morning.

QuestionText: The lymphatic system collects
Options: A) Excess tissue fluid and returns it to the blood
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Lymph capillaries collect interstitial fluid (leaked from blood capillaries) and return it to the blood via lymph vessels.

QuestionText: The fluid found between cells (tissue fluid) is called
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Some plasma leaks from blood capillaries into spaces between cells forming tissue fluid, which bathes the cells.

QuestionText: The force that makes blood flow is generated by
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: The heart is a muscular pump; its contractions generate blood pressure that drives circulation.

QuestionText: Pulmonary circulation is the circuit that carries blood
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Pulmonary circulation: right ventricle → lungs (for oxygenation) → left atrium.

QuestionText: Systemic circulation carries blood
Options: A) Between heart and body tissues
C) Between heart and liver only
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Systemic circulation: left ventricle → aorta → all body tissues → vena cava → right atrium.

QuestionText: Arteries have thick elastic muscular walls because
Options: A) They withstand high blood pressure from the heart
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Arterial walls have thick smooth muscle and elastic tissue to withstand and smooth out high pressure pulses.

QuestionText: Veins have ___ to prevent backflow of blood
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Veins contain semi-lunar valves that prevent backward flow of blood under low pressure.

QuestionText: The biconcave shape of red blood cells
Options: A) Increases surface area for O2 diffusion
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Biconcave disc shape of RBCs maximises surface area to volume ratio, enabling efficient O2 and CO2 exchange.

QuestionText: RBCs lack a nucleus in mature form so that
Options: A) They carry more haemoglobin and are more flexible
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Enucleated mature RBCs have maximum space for haemoglobin and can squeeze through narrow capillaries.

QuestionText: The heartbeat sound (lub-dub) is caused by
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Lub = AV valves (tricuspid, mitral) closing; Dub = semilunar valves (aortic, pulmonary) closing.

QuestionText: Stethoscope is used to
Options: A) Listen to heart and lung sounds
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: A stethoscope amplifies heart sounds (lub-dub) and breath sounds for medical examination.

QuestionText: Blood groups (ABO system) are classified based on
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: ABO blood groups are determined by the presence of antigens (A, B, both, or neither) on the RBC surface.

QuestionText: Universal blood donor is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: O- blood has no ABO or Rh antigens, so it can be given to any recipient in emergencies: universal donor.

QuestionText: Universal blood recipient is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: AB+ individuals have all ABO and Rh antigens; they can receive any blood type.

QuestionText: The main excretory product in human urine is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Urea is the main nitrogenous excretory product in humans, produced in the liver from amino acid metabolism.

QuestionText: Deficiency of haemoglobin or RBCs causes
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Anaemia: insufficient haemoglobin or RBCs → reduced O2 transport → fatigue, pallor, breathlessness.

QuestionText: Systolic pressure is the pressure
Options: A) When the heart contracts (ventricles contract)
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Systolic: pressure during ventricular contraction. Diastolic: pressure during relaxation. Normal: ~120/80 mmHg.

QuestionText: Translocation in plants refers to
Options: A) Transport of sugars through phloem
B) Transport of water through xylem
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Translocation: movement of photosynthates (sucrose) through phloem from source (leaves) to sink (roots, fruits).

QuestionText: The movement of water from high concentration to low concentration through a semi-permeable membrane is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Osmosis: movement of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution.

QuestionText: Pericardium is
Options: A) The protective sac surrounding the heart
C) The inner lining of heart
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: The pericardium is a double-walled sac that encases the heart, providing protection and lubrication.

QuestionText: Plasma proteins like albumin are important for
Options: A) Maintaining blood osmotic pressure (oncotic pressure)
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Albumin (most abundant plasma protein) maintains osmotic pressure, preventing excess fluid from leaking out of capillaries.

QuestionText: The term cardiac output means
Options: A) Volume of blood pumped by heart per minute
D) Volume of one heartbeat only
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Cardiac Output = Heart Rate × Stroke Volume. Normal CO ~ 5 L/min at rest.

QuestionText: A sphygmomanometer measures
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: A sphygmomanometer (blood pressure cuff) measures systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

QuestionText: The circulatory system in earthworm is
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Earthworms have a closed circulatory system with 5 pairs of aortic arches (pseudo-hearts).

QuestionText: Insects have an ___ circulatory system
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Insects have an open circulatory system; haemolymph flows freely around organs in haemocoel, not in vessels.

QuestionText: Haemolymph in insects differs from blood because
Options: A) It does NOT transport oxygen (gas exchange by tracheal system)
D) It flows in closed vessels
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: In insects, gas exchange occurs via tracheal tubes, not blood. Haemolymph transports nutrients and wastes only.

QuestionText: The beating of the heart is regulated by the
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: The SA node in the right atrium initiates each heartbeat: the natural pacemaker of the heart.

QuestionText: Oedema (swelling of tissues) can be caused by
Options: A) Low blood albumin (reduced oncotic pressure) or blocked lymph drainage
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Without sufficient albumin (or with blocked lymphatics), fluid accumulates in tissue spaces: oedema.

QuestionText: Atherosclerosis refers to
Options: A) Hardening/narrowing of arteries due to plaque deposits
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Atherosclerosis: fatty plaques deposit on artery inner walls, reducing lumen size and elasticity, increasing heart attack risk.

QuestionText: In plants, apoplast pathway for water movement is through
Options: A) Cell walls and intercellular spaces (not through membranes)
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: Apoplast pathway: water moves through cell walls without crossing membranes, until blocked by the Casparian strip in endodermis.

QuestionText: Double circulation in humans means
Options: A) Blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit
Topic: Biology - Transportation in Animals and Plants
Explanation: In double circulation: pulmonary circuit (heart → lungs → heart) + systemic circuit (heart → body → heart). Blood passes through heart twice.
